findings: C7: '## Core features' runs to about 42,000 characters, far past the 2,500-character point at which run_rubric slices a section for the judge. The tail reaches the agent in full. Accepted deliberately: window_lint (G33) fails nothing on length, the judged criteria are self-contained and carry their own evaluation_rule, judge_score never touches reward, and the companion's route set cannot be stated in 2,500 characters without deleting requirements.
A1: eleven H2 sections are present. '## Build plan' is omitted at baseline per 2.1 and '## Front-end specification' carries the long visual specification, which is the unbudgeted home 4 names for it.

D5: every companion subsection is reconciled in the carry table in spec/00-decisions.md. Two are carried INVERTED on purpose and are recorded there: sign-in is implemented by this application rather than delegated to a hosted identity provider, because no identity provider exists in this environment; and the reference's soft not-found is replaced by a real not-found status, which the companion itself instructs.

S2: the PRD lists ten must-have features rather than three to six. config/corpus-targets.yaml companion_feature_cap raises the cap to [6, 10] for a companion-backed task, and records that the three-to-six cap deletes exactly the content a real source document supplies. Recorded as conforming to the companion cap.

S5: 04-uiux-brief.md carries the companion's measured hexes, type scale, motion values, accessibility bar and mode commitment under 'Measured values, authoring reference only'. They stay in spec/: the settled number rule (A5) forbids a hex, a millisecond or a pixel in instruction.md.

S6: 05-backend-schema.md names the engine construct per invariant under 'Storage-level invariants, authoring reference only'. instruction.md carries the observable invariant instead, as INV9 and G43 require.

DEP-015, DEP-016 and DEP-017 are NOT-APPLICABLE: the drawn stack is Python, so there is no compiled-language build stage, no host module cache to copy and no JRE to install. BP-005 and BP-008 are NOT-APPLICABLE for the same reason: a single-stage glibc Debian base is the correct shape for this runtime.

The ARCH family is NOT-APPLICABLE beyond ARCH-001: the image is pinned by an explicit multi-architecture version tag, declares TARGETARCH without reading it, downloads nothing at build time, and carries no comments at all, so there is no per-architecture asset, branch, digest or note to inspect.

BLD-002, BLD-004 and BLD-007 are NOT-APPLICABLE: the image installs the runtime and the grader set only. The application source does not exist at build time, so there is no lockfile to respect and no COPY order to get wrong. BP-004 is NOT-APPLICABLE: nothing is downloaded outside the package managers.
ENV-003 and ENV-004 are NOT-APPLICABLE: the image declares no VOLUME and no ENTRYPOINT, and no source requires either.
SEC-005 is NOT-APPLICABLE: no secret-bearing variable is set with ENV; every credential reaches the container from task.toml at run time.
DEP-001 is NOT-APPLICABLE: the TRD declares no package manager beyond the language default, and pip is that default.

CON-004 is NOT-APPLICABLE: the reference Dockerfiles under tasks/ are pre-kit regression baselines and carry comments the current gates forbid, so their layout is not the convention this file is measured against.

RC-12: every criterion that a pytest assertion could decide was moved to the pytest channel during authoring; the fifteen that remain are appearance and flow judgements over rendered surfaces, and channel_lint confirms none of their checklist items is claimed by pytest or by a browser substep.

The checklist carries 315 items across ten section codes, every id sequential, every item citing its source line, and the coverage ledger reconciles against the obligation-sentence count of every instruction section. checklist_qc.py reports the structural half clean.
TAX-008 is NOT-APPLICABLE: global archetype uniqueness cannot be decided from one bundle. The mint ledger at the output root holds the claim.

SIGN-001, SIGN-002 and SIGN-003 are NOT-APPLICABLE: the [signoff] table was retired on 2026-09-15 and the three checks are marked deprecated in the prompt's own registry. SIGN-004 supersedes them and passes.
BENCH-002 is NOT-APPLICABLE: this is not a trivial or smoke task, so the Trivial tier does not apply. BENCH-001 carries the Standard tier and passes.

BENCH-003, BENCH-005 and INT-007 are NOT-APPLICABLE: difficulty is the empty placeholder, because calibration writes it and the kit never does, so there is no declared difficulty for the budget to be consistent with.
TAX-006 is NOT-APPLICABLE: language is python, not any.
INST-007 is NOT-APPLICABLE: instruction.md is present.
SVC-008 is NOT-APPLICABLE: no add-on slot beyond the core three is declared.
